pr_title: Bluetooth: gatt: Add support for automatic ATT MTU Exchange
pr_body:
This adds support for automatic ATT MTU Exchange that will be done right after the connection has been established.
This ensures the ATT MTU Exchange request will not be sent more than once. As the improvement the code follows Core 5.3 recommendation to skip MTU Exchange procedure if already performed by peer.

Fixes: #43946
pr_comments:
Changes made:

- Excluded `ATT_MTU_EXCHANGE_*` flags when `CONFIG_BT_GATT_CLIENT` is not set
- Added warning when auto MTU Exchange failed

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Automatic ATT MTU negotiation
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, the ATT MTU Exchange is initiated by calling `bt_gatt_exchange_mtu`. Having multiple GATT Client-based profiles that require MTU to be other than default 23, shows a need of MTU exchange procedure improvement if all of the profiles will call the API method.
Current API allows the ATT MTU Exchange to be sent multiple times. This violates the Core Spec 5.2 Vol 3 Part F 3.4.2.1 ATT_EXCHANGE_MTU_REQ: "This request shall only be sent once during a connection by the client."

**Describe the solution you'd like**
1. Allow the client to perform ATT MTU Exchange only once during connection.
2. As improvement, the stack could skip sending ATT Exchange MTU if already exchanged by peer as Core recommends:
Core 5.3 | Vol 3, Part F 3.4.2.2 ATT_EXCHANGE_MTU_RSP: "If MTU is exchanged in one direction, that is sufficient for both directions."
3. To have a Kconfig option that if enabled, the GATT Client could initiate the MTU Exchange automatically.

review_comments: Looks like a misunderstanding. `bt_gatt_exchange_mtu` shall only be done as a client, thus it should be guarded with `CONFIG_BT_GATT_CLIENT`. It is true that it isn't related to subscriptions, but that doesn't change that this would (probably) still be the correct way of doing it.
